meta.title: Piuma — Instagram every week, under your control
meta.description: Piuma drafts your posts to your plan, learns from your own Instagram Insights what works and when, and publishes only once you approve. Data stays in the EU.
meta.keywords: Piuma, Instagram scheduling, Instagram management, social media for business, Instagram Insights, SMM agency, Carbon Stealth
meta.ogAlt: Piuma — an Instagram content engine by Carbon Stealth VCC

hero.eyebrow: Official Instagram API · data in the EU
hero.title: Posts every week.
hero.lead: Piuma drafts your posts to your plan, learns from your own Insights what works and when, and you just approve. Nothing reaches Instagram without a person.
hero.note: You connect your account through Meta’s official sign-in and it stays yours. Piuma never sees your password and never creates profiles.
hero.shotAlt: The Piuma dashboard: drafts awaiting review, upcoming posts, per-account quotas

proof.reviewBody: Drafts arrive ready, but nothing is published until someone on your team presses “Approve”.
proof.label: Why Piuma
proof.learnBody: It looks at what earns engagement, and when, on your account — not at averages from the internet.
proof.euTitle: your data stays in the EU
proof.euBody: Our own server in Europe, encrypted tokens and a full log of who did what.

how.title: Three steps, no surprises
how.lead: Every post takes the same path. There is no button that skips a step.
how.step1Body: You write it, a colleague does, or our agent does from the page’s plan. The result is always a draft — nothing more.
how.step2Body: You review the text, the image and the time. Built-in checks stop empty or overlong captions, anything that looks like a password, and too many hashtags.
how.step3Body: At the scheduled time, through the official API, retrying on temporary errors. If Instagram refuses, you see the reason in the panel.
how.guardTitle: What if the agent gets it wrong?
how.guardBody: It can’t publish. Its key only reaches drafts — the path to approval simply doesn’t exist for it.

panel.title: Everything on one screen
panel.lead: What’s waiting for review, what’s scheduled, what went out and what failed — and why.
panel.point1: Clear statuses with an icon and a word — readable at a glance.
panel.point2: Seven roles — from viewer to owner. Everyone sees and does exactly their part.
panel.point3: Two-factor sign-in with an authenticator app — no SMS.
panel.point4: Works on your phone too — approve on the go.
panel.shotAlt: The post list in Piuma with status chips: draft, approved, scheduled, published, rejected
panel.composeAlt: Writing a draft in Piuma: by hand on the left, model suggestions on the right

autopilot.title: An autopilot that learns — and doesn’t guess
autopilot.lead: Once a week Piuma prepares the drafts for the pages it manages and reads your own Instagram Insights: which time, format and topic earn more engagement. Approval stays human.
autopilot.point1: The plan is yours: how many posts, what share of Reels, which times and topics, what to avoid.
autopilot.point2: It only uses your photos and videos — it never invents material.
autopilot.point3: It recommends only once there’s enough data. Until then it says, honestly, “too early”.
autopilot.shotAlt: A 30-day trend in Piuma: followers, reach, views and engaged accounts
autopilot.point4: Ready-made caption variants for Facebook, TikTok, LinkedIn and X.

security.title: Security that doesn’t rely on good intentions
security.lead: Piuma holds access to other people’s accounts. That’s why the protections are built into the code, not left to a setting.
security.item1Body: Its requests are signed and valid for minutes, and its key only reaches drafts.
security.item2Body: Instagram tokens and keys are encrypted (AES-256-GCM) and never end up in logs.
security.item3Body: Every action is recorded — who, what and from where. Tampering with an old entry breaks the chain and shows at once.
security.item4Body: App codes (TOTP), passwords hashed with Argon2id, and sessions you can revoke instantly.
security.item5Body: Seven access levels. No one manages someone with an equal or higher role.
security.item6Body: Our own database on a European server — no hosted CMS or third-party platform in between.

langs.title: The panel speaks the team’s language

faq.title: Common questions
faq.q1: Can Piuma create an Instagram account?
faq.a1: No. Meta’s terms forbid automated account creation. The account is made by hand, switched to a professional one and connected through the official OAuth.
faq.q2: Can an agent publish on its own?
faq.a2: No. The agent only reaches drafts. Approving and publishing simply don’t exist for it — there’s nothing to get around.
faq.q3: What happens if Instagram refuses a post?
faq.a3: Piuma retries on temporary errors, and the reason for the refusal is shown in the panel next to the post, together with the number of attempts.
faq.q4: Where do the performance numbers come from?
faq.a4: From your own Instagram Insights, pulled every night. Piuma doesn’t invent metrics — and gives no recommendation until there’s enough data.
faq.a5: Piuma uses the official Instagram Platform API — the route Meta provides for publishing tools — and tracks the account’s publishing quota. It doesn’t automate logins, likes or follows.
faq.a6: Seven roles with different permissions. Approval takes at least a reviewer, and authors can’t approve their own drafts.
faq.a7: No. You upload photos, set the plan and approve drafts in the panel. The server, updates and security are on us.
faq.q8: Does it work for several brands?
faq.a8: Yes. Each brand has its own plan, its own Instagram accounts and its own media library — all in the same panel.

who.title: Who Piuma is for
who.lead: For anyone who wants to show up on Instagram regularly without writing every post themselves — and without losing control.
who.smallBody: Café, shop, studio, salon. Upload your photos once, Piuma prepares the week, and you just review and approve.
who.agencyBody: Many brands in one panel — each with its own plan, accounts and media library.
who.teamBody: Tone of voice and off-limits topics are part of the plan. Seven roles, and a draft’s author can’t approve it alone.

learn.topicWhy: the difference is still within the noise
learn.note: A verdict appears only with a clear lead of at least 15%. The measure is engagement relative to reach — not raw reach, which grows with the account.

keys.title: Agent keys
keys.subtitle: Machine access for our agents. Requests are HMAC-signed (the secret never travels), with a timestamp and a nonce against replay. The scope is narrow by construction: an agent can read and create drafts — approval, scheduling and publishing do not exist for keys.
keys.created: Key “{name}” created — the secret is shown only now
keys.createdHint: Put them on the agent's machine in a file with mode 600 (e.g. /etc/piuma/agent.env) and hand them to tools/social/piuma.mjs. Never in a repo, a chat or a log.
keys.name: Name
